title: George Lasry’s partial decipherments of Siena nos. 20 and 23 (DECODE R4808, R4811)

steps.what: The existing siena1421 collection survey records unsuccessful homophonic/null-aware attempts on nos. 20 and 23; this contribution does not rerun or claim those attempts.
Local CTTS review records document removal of overlapping selections and revision of compound and look-alike sign classes. The submitted snapshot is 4,247 cipher selections in two documents.

Following CTTS transcription, GPT-6 Astra solved the cipher, as confirmed by George Lasry. Local analyses of no. 23 reconstruct word/letter-group signs, nulls and repeated personal-name codes, with image checking and application to no. 20. The supplied editions retain unresolved readings.

Recounted the current key/transcriptions, regenerated the visual key, preserved the supplied editions and translations, and verified only R4811 L49:39–51:24: 108 signs yield 109 letters matching the supplied edition after spacing, punctuation, accents and u/v normalization. This selected excerpt does not establish complete-reading accuracy.

Checked Tartaglia, Ladislaus, Rodolfo III da Varano, Ludovico Migliorati and a possible Gattola identification in linked sources. A Ladislaus-era setting is plausible, but year, camp location and unresolved names remain unproved; no complete printed plaintext was located in the limited searches.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 108 tokens, 32 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -2.102 per letter; random keys -3.65 (z 6.8); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.381 (mean -2.462, z 5.2); annealer on the real text -2.295. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.102; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.295 Scope: only the deliberately selected 108-sign excerpt, not the complete key or the supplied editions. Language-model normalization reduces the 109 literal letters to 106 scored letters.

outcome.method_basis: Transcribed with CTTS, then solved by GPT-6 Astra, as confirmed by George Lasry. Recovery used ciphertext patterns and original cleartext framing, without a historical decipherment or matched external key.
outcome.fraction_read_source: counts.json: 4,033 unbracketed assignments / 4,074 non-null cipher occurrences; excludes 173 provisional nulls and 11 noncipher selections. Assignment coverage, not meaningful-reading accuracy.

credits.note: Directed the work and supplied the CTTS material, partial Italian readings and English translations. Transcribed with CTTS, then solved by GPT-6 Astra; contribution preparation and checks by Codex.

gaps.item: Personal-name codes fat, o+, ovo and historical identities/year
gaps.detail: Names1–3 unidentified; Tartaglia supported internally; year and all correspondents not independently fixed.

gaps.item: b1, 3bar, Fom, y3, ta, s2, m2 and h/s fork variants
Lacunae, subscription and doubtful words in supplied editions
gaps.detail: Editorial readings retained as supplied, not asserted new key assignments.
Current working transcription needs further occurrence-level checks.

outcome.notes: No complete mechanical decoding included. Statistical validation, if recorded, applies only to the deliberately selected 108-sign excerpt, not either whole edition. No exact year, first-break claim or complete key claimed.

prior.where: The earlier collection survey records unsuccessful work on this pair. No historical decipherment or external key was used in this recovery; no first-publication claim is made.

human: George Lasry supplied the cipher images, directed the work and provided the Italian readings and English translations. He confirms that the cipher was transcribed with CTTS, then solved by GPT-6 Astra. Codex prepared the PR, checked the inventory and short excerpt, and added limited historical context.
